messages.content:
You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in a body-centered tetragonal setting of space group I-42m (number 121, Hall symbol I -4 2), but the supplied input cell is a nonstandard one: all three input lattice vectors have equal length 6.07880892 Å, with interaxial angles α = β = 120.94789772° and γ = 88.36588716°. The input cell contains ten atoms with the declared composition K₁Sr₁Bi₂O₆. Fractional coordinates in this input frame are related to the standard I-42m frame by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0) and the matrix P has first row (−1/2, 1/2, 1/2), second row (1/2, −1/2, 1/2), and third row (1/2, 1/2, −1/2); thus each standard coordinate is formed from half-sum combinations of the input coordinates, for example x_std = (−x_in + y_in + z_in)/2 and analogously for the other two components. No origin translation is applied, and no positional corrections beyond rounding are needed: the reported values are given to six decimal places and the precision-correction list is empty.

In the standard frame the ten-atom input cell corresponds to the conventional body-centered cell with five independent crystallographic orbits. Potassium occupies the fixed Wyckoff site 2a at (0, 0, 0), giving two K atoms per conventional cell related by the body-centering translation. Strontium occupies the fixed site 2b at (0, 0, 1/2), likewise doubled by the I-centering to two Sr atoms. Bismuth sits on the fixed fourfold site 4d at (0, 1/2, 1/4), so the four Bi atoms lie at the midpoints of cell edges in the ab plane at one-quarter height along c, together with their centering equivalents.

The oxygen atoms split into two inequivalent sublattices. One is the fixed fourfold site 4c at (0, 1/2, 0), placing four O atoms on edge-midpoint positions in the basal plane. The other is the eightfold general-position family 8i with coordinate relation (x, x, z), whose representative lies at x = 0.190664 (more precisely 0.19066449999999996 before rounding) and z = 0.7328105; the two equal coordinates constrain these atoms to lie on the diagonal vertical mirror planes of the tetragonal structure, and the full orbit of eight is generated from this single pair of free parameters by the site symmetry and body centering. Together the 2 + 2 + 4 + 8 + 4 atoms of the conventional cell reproduce, after the inverse frame transformation, the ten-atom nonstandard input cell with its K₁Sr₁Bi₂O₆ content.
